prompt: A team wants to edit Databricks code on feature branches and synchronize it with a remote Git repository. Which workspace feature fits?

options.text: Databricks Git folders
Delta Lake time travel
DBFS mounts
Unity Catalog table lineage

explanation: Git folders, formerly Repos, support Git-based branches, commits, pulls, and pushes. Table history tracks data changes rather than code changes. Commit and push code before creating a pull request in the Git provider.

prompt: What do Declarative Automation Bundles provide for a data engineering team?

options.text: Versioned configuration and code for reproducible deployment of jobs, pipelines, and related workspace resources
A copy of every Delta data file embedded in YAML
A substitute for testing deployment changes
An automatically granted admin identity for every developer

explanation: Bundles, formerly Declarative Automation Bundles, package resource definitions and code for development and CI/CD. They integrate with Git and the Databricks CLI. They do not replace tests or automatically grant privileges.

sources.label: Supplied academy notes: Declarative Automation Bundles

prompt: What is the databricks CLI used for?

options.text: To interact with Databricks programmatically: manage clusters, jobs, workspaces, and run commands from local machines or CI/CD pipelines
Only for browsing the web
To create SQL dashboards only
To manage user passwords only

explanation: The Databricks CLI enables programmatic interaction with Databricks: create/manage clusters, submit jobs, import/export notebooks, manage Unity Catalog objects, deploy Declarative Automation Bundles, and more. It is essential for automation, CI/CD pipelines, and scripting Databricks operations.

prompt: How can you deploy a Databricks job to multiple workspaces (dev, staging, prod)?

options.text: Use Declarative Automation Bundles with environment-specific configuration files and CI/CD pipelines
Manually recreate the job in each workspace
It is not possible
Copy the job ID between workspaces

explanation: Declarative Automation Bundles (DABs) define jobs as YAML files with environment-specific overrides. Use the same bundle with different target environments (databricks bundle deploy -t dev/staging/prod). CI/CD pipelines automate testing and promotion. This ensures consistency across environments.

sources.label: Supplied academy notes: Declarative Automation Bundles

prompt: What is the databricks bundle deploy command used for?

options.text: To deploy Databricks resources defined in an Declarative Automation Bundle to a target workspace
To delete bundles
To create notebooks
To schedule jobs only

explanation: databricks bundle deploy deploys resources defined in databricks.yml (jobs, pipelines, notebooks, queries) to the specified target workspace. It validates the bundle, creates/updates resources, and handles dependencies. This enables infrastructure-as-code deployment from local development or CI/CD pipelines.

sources.label: Supplied academy notes: Declarative Automation Bundles

prompt: What is the databricks bundle validate command used for?

options.text: To check the syntax and configuration of a Declarative Automation Bundle without deploying
To run jobs
To delete bundles
To create clusters

explanation: databricks bundle validate checks the bundle configuration for errors: valid YAML syntax, correct resource definitions, valid references, and environment configurations. It catches issues before deployment. Run this in CI/CD pipelines and before deploy to ensure bundle correctness.

prompt: A bundle job has already been deployed. What does databricks bundle run -t prod daily_etl do?

options.text: Starts the named deployed bundle resource for the prod target
Deploys all changed resources automatically and then starts the job
Runs every job in every workspace
Only validates YAML without executing any resource

explanation: bundle run runs a specified bundle resource; deploy changes first with bundle deploy. validate checks configuration. Selecting a target controls the environment to which the command applies.

prompt: A developer has committed a notebook fix on a feature branch in a Databricks Git folder. What makes it available for remote review?

options.text: Push the branch and create a pull request in the Git provider
Run RESTORE on a Delta table
Export the job run logs to a volume
Change the production workspace host in YAML without pushing

explanation: A local commit records history in the Git folder. Pushing publishes commits to the remote branch, where a pull request supports review before merging. Notebook history and table time travel do not publish a Git branch.

sources.label: Supplied academy notes: Declarative Automation Bundles

prompt: One bundle must write to dev and prod catalogs using the same code. Which pattern fits?

options.text: Define a catalog variable and override its value in each target
Hardcode prod catalog names in every notebook
Copy the production notebook manually after every edit
Replace the workspace metastore on every deployment

explanation: Bundle variables and target configuration let the same resource definitions and code use environment-specific values. Keep the target selection explicit in CI/CD.

sources.label: Supplied academy notes: Declarative Automation Bundles

prompt: A bundle defines a variable named catalog. Which substitution references its configured value?

options.text: ${var.catalog}
${catalog.var}
{{ input.catalog }}
catalog.schema.table

explanation: Bundle variable substitution uses ${var.name}. For each task inputs use a different dynamic reference syntax. A Unity Catalog three-part identifier names a data object, not a bundle variable.

sources.label: Supplied academy notes: Declarative Automation Bundles

prompt: Dev and prod deployments use different Databricks workspaces. Where should the environment-specific host be configured?

options.text: In the appropriate bundle target workspace configuration
Inside the SQL SELECT list for every query
In the data table transaction log
Only in a notebook display label

explanation: Targets can override workspace settings and resource configuration. The selected target must resolve to the intended host and authenticated identity. Verify the deployment summary before promotion.

sources.label: Supplied academy notes: Declarative Automation Bundles

prompt: Which command sequence validates a prod target, deploys its resources, and then runs daily_etl?

options.text: databricks bundle validate -t prod; databricks bundle deploy -t prod; databricks bundle run -t prod daily_etl
databricks bundle run -t prod daily_etl; assume this deploys every change automatically
databricks bundle validate -t prod; assume this executes all job tasks
databricks bundle destroy -t prod; assume this deploys the resources

explanation: validate checks configuration, deploy updates resources, and run starts a named resource. Use the same intended target throughout. Running a resource is distinct from deploying changed code and definitions.

sources.label: Supplied academy notes: Declarative Automation Bundles

prompt: A tested commit is ready for production. Which deployment process provides reproducible promotion?

options.text: Deploy that reviewed commit with the prod target and controlled configuration
Edit the production notebook manually to resemble the dev version
Deploy whichever developer branch was modified most recently
Copy a job run ID from dev into prod

explanation: Promote a known reviewed code revision through environment targets. Bundles define resources and configuration alongside code. Manual recreation and mutable unreviewed source weaken deployment repeatability.

sources.label: Supplied academy notes: Declarative Automation Bundles

prompt: A developer needs to make a change without immediately modifying the shared main branch. What should they do in the Git folder?

options.text: Create or switch to a feature branch, make the change, and commit it
Run VACUUM on the code repository
Use Delta time travel to version the notebook source
Change the job owner to create a Git branch

explanation: Git folders expose branch operations for code development. Feature branches support review before merging into the shared branch. Delta versioning concerns table data, not Git code history.

sources.label: Supplied academy notes: Declarative Automation Bundles

prompt: A teammate has merged a change into the remote branch used by a Git folder. How should the developer obtain it?

options.text: Pull the remote changes after handling local modifications appropriately
Run OPTIMIZE on the notebook
Only commit the current local files without fetching changes
Grant SELECT on the repository

explanation: Pull synchronizes remote commits into the local Git working copy. Resolve or preserve local modifications and conflicts deliberately. Committing alone does not fetch teammates changes.

sources.label: Supplied academy notes: Declarative Automation Bundles

prompt: bundle validate succeeds. Which statement about readiness is correct?

options.text: Configuration validation passed, but workload tests and runtime authorization still need appropriate verification
Every SQL query is guaranteed to return the intended business result
Production execution has already completed
Every destination privilege has been granted automatically

explanation: Configuration validation is useful before deployment. It cannot prove every transformation result, source availability, or runtime permission. CI/CD should also verify the behavior of the workload.

sources.label: Supplied academy notes: Declarative Automation Bundles

prompt: A CI/CD pipeline must deploy resources without depending on one employee account. Which identity fits?

options.text: A service principal with the required scoped deployment permissions
Every developer using a shared personal password
An anonymous SQL warehouse user
A column mask UDF

explanation: A service principal provides an identity for automation. Grant only the required privileges and configure supported non-interactive authentication. Deployment identity and job Run as identity should both be explicit.

sources.label: Supplied academy notes: Declarative Automation Bundles

prompt: A job schedule was changed manually in prod but the bundle still defines the old schedule. What should the team do to maintain reproducibility?

options.text: Record the intended schedule in the versioned bundle configuration and redeploy through the normal process
Rely permanently on undocumented manual drift
Delete all job history
Use a column tag to version the schedule

explanation: Resource definitions should describe the intended deployed configuration. Capture approved changes in source control so future deployments do not unexpectedly restore an older setting.

sources.label: Supplied academy notes: Declarative Automation Bundles

prompt: A bundle catalog variable is resolved during deployment. Can passing a different job runtime parameter automatically change that already-resolved bundle variable?

options.text: No; deployment variables and job runtime parameters have separate evaluation contexts
Yes; every runtime parameter rewrites databricks.yml
Yes; a notebook widget always changes the CLI target
Only when the job uses an external table

explanation: Bundle substitutions are resolved for deployment or CLI operations. Job parameters are values supplied to task execution. Wire the desired runtime configurability into task parameters explicitly.

sources.label: Supplied academy notes: Declarative Automation Bundles

prompt: Which files should be reviewed together when a notebook change also alters its production task dependencies?

options.text: The transformation code and the bundle resource configuration
Only an exported screenshot of the job graph
Only the latest table data files
Only a user token copied into the repository

explanation: Bundles keep workload resources and code together for review and deployment. Changing dependencies affects execution behavior and should be reviewed with the code that relies on those dependencies.
